en.html:
Acting for the Lord of Horigoe in Fudaraku proved no great difficulty. Not as great as I had prepared for, at any rate.

There were several reasons. Chief among them was Chachamaru’s support team.

They served their suddenly appointed lieutenant colonel of unknown origins without warmth, but with a measure of fidelity. An extraordinary arrangement. Outward obedience and inward opposition would have been the natural response.

Perhaps that was the character of the Horigoe administration. Serving Chachamaru might require a habit of obeying even abnormal instructions without thinking.

Or perhaps she had simply warned them before leaving. Either way, I did not expect their faithful service to last. Nor did I worry over it.

Acting lord, deputy, lieutenant colonel: temporary conveniences. Laboring to build excellent military relationships would be a waste. We needed to get along for the necessary period. No lifetime subscription was being requested.

I asked their opinions on the many matters brought in daily; they supplied them. Experienced military bureaucrats, their judgment was rarely wrong.

Half my work was conversation. The other half, signatures and seals.

Monotonous, wholly unoriginal administration. I knew a general could nevertheless function that way. A general determined to display personality might be useful in an emergency; in peacetime, he could become everybody’s burden.

During my conscript service, I had spent a period as a headquarters orderly. The general I served belonged to the unoriginal school. Watching him closely, I saw him listen to others’ ideas far more often than producing his own.

Yet he was called a master of military administration. Nobody governed occupied territory better. After his transfer, a brilliant general replaced him. Before long, the local people rebelled.

Being brilliant, the successor would not listen to his staff. He executed his own ideas throughout. As far as results were concerned, there was little doubt which method had been correct.

So I now imitated General Higuchi. Irony and retaliation both: six years ago he had resisted Rokuhara’s rebellion and been executed for it.

普陀楽における堀越公方の代行は、実際、さほどの
困難もなく務まっていた。
　覚悟していたほどではない、という意味だが。

　それには幾つかの理由がある。
　特に大きいのは、茶々丸が用意した<ruby>補佐集団<rt>サポートチーム</rt></ruby>の存在
だろう。

　出自不明の俄か中佐に、彼らは淡々と、しかし一応
忠実に仕えてくれる。
　……奇妙といえば、これほど奇妙な話もない。面従
腹背の姿勢になって当然のところだ。

　あるいは、これは堀越公方府の性格なのか。
　茶々丸のような人間のもとで幕僚を務めるためには、
上司の時として異常な指示に対しても<ruby>考えず<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>服従する、
そんな習性を身に付ける必要があったのかもしれない。

　それとも単に、茶々丸が出がけに釘を刺していった
のか。
　どちらにしても彼らの俺への<ruby>忠勤<rt>・・</rt></ruby>が長続きするとは
思えないが、その点に関して俺は気に病まなかった。

　堀越公方の代行は勿論、副官も中佐も一時の方便に
過ぎないのである。
　軍内における良好な人間関係の構築を目指して努力
するなど、無駄であった。

　彼らとは必要な間だけうまくやれればそれで良い。

　日々持ち込まれる幾多の案件について、俺は彼らに
意見を求め、彼らは求めに応じて発言する。
　熟練した軍官僚である彼らの判断に、間違いはまず
無かった。

　俺の仕事は半分がた、彼らとの対話である。
　残りは署名と捺印だ。

　単調で独創性の欠片もない執務姿勢だが、将帥とは
それでも務まる事を俺は知っていた。
　むしろ個性を発揮したがる将帥の方が、非常事態の
折ならともかく、平時には煙たがられる事も。

　徴兵されて軍にいた頃の一時期、司令部付当番兵を
務めた。そのとき仕えた相手が無個性型の将軍だった。
　彼の振舞いを間近でつぶさに見たが、自分で知恵を
出すより他人の知恵を聞く方がずっと多かったと思う。

　しかしそれで、彼は軍政の名人と呼ばれていた。彼
ほど占領地を上手に治めた者はいなかった。
　彼はやがて転任し、代わって秀才型の将軍が来たが、
その新体制は程なく地元民の反乱を招いた。

　秀才ゆえ幕僚の意見を聞こうとせず、自分の考えで
全て断行した結果だった。
　将軍としてどちらの姿勢が正しかったか、少なくと
も結果論の範囲では疑問の余地がない。

　だから俺は今、あの樋口という名の将軍を模倣する。
　ある意味で、これは皮肉であり意趣返しだ――樋口
将軍は六年前、六波羅の反逆劇に対して抵抗したすえ
処刑されているのだから。

ｅｔｃ／補佐"May we proceed with this matter as it stands?"
Kageaki"I leave it to you."
ｅｔｃ／補佐"Sir."
Kageaki"Where is the inventory breakdown?"
ｅｔｃ／補佐"Here."
Kageaki"...The timber falls short of the ordered quantity."
ｅｔｃ／補佐"Yes. Some was diverted to castle-gate repairs. We are short by that amount."
ｅｔｃ／補佐"Shall we procure replacements urgently?"
Kageaki"Procure them, yes. No need to force the matter. The original order appears to allow a considerable surplus."
ｅｔｃ／補佐"...Indeed."
Kageaki"Even allowing for the venue’s size, what we have should suffice. Leave it for now. Add the shortage to the next order when another requirement arises."
ｅｔｃ／補佐"Sir. It shall be done."

en.html:
Preparations for the appointment ceremony were underway. Perhaps the Lord of Sasagawa’s threats had worked: Kyoto’s attitude had improved, and Kuniuji Ashikaga’s appointment approached its final countdown.

The Horigoe administration had been assigned construction of the venue. A small piece of luck. In my company days I had done this sort of work to the point of exhaustion.

There was ample scope for my accumulated know-how. That luck also helped me maintain a convincing acting lord’s face.

Today brought particularly many construction matters. I examined each, accepted advice, and dealt with it.

城内では現在、宣下式典の準備が進められている。
　篠川公方の威圧策の効果あってか、京都情勢が好転
し、足利邦氏への大将領宣下が秒読み段階に入ったの
を受けての事だ。

　式典会場の設営は、堀越公方府の担当となった。
　これは小さな幸運と呼べたろう。会社員時代、俺は
この手の仕事なら飽きるほどこなしてきている。

　蓄えた<ruby>技術知識<rt>ノウハウ</rt></ruby>を活用する場には事欠かなかった。
　俺がそれなりに公方代行らしい面をしていられるの
には、この幸運もある。

　今日は特に、設営関係の案件が多かった。
　一つ一つ吟味し、助言を受けながら処理してゆく。

en.html:
Surrounded by bewildered workers and guards, I received the report. On the surface, simple enough.

Some materials had disappeared from storage. Not because they had been carried to the proper place and used.

That had already been checked. They had vanished without any sign of use.

Clearly, their removal had followed an improper procedure.
